notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Plates have an orange dot on the left side; this design is unique in Europe.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: The main language is a Romance one close to Spanish and French; an i for 'and' instead of y is the giveaway, and more words end in consonants.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: The word for street is carrer.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Guardrails carry yellow reflectors, found in Europe only here, in Spain and in Belgium.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Bollards with an orange reflector appear occasionally on the main highways.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Kilometre markers show CG and CS road numbers.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Snow poles are made of wood and come in various colours.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Traffic cones are yellow and turquoise-green across the whole country.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Almost all coverage is generation 3 with a medium-short antenna, shot in October, so deciduous trees show autumn colours.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Stone buildings are found almost everywhere; similar ones exist in the French and Spanish Pyrenees.

notes.subject: coverage
notes.text: Lots of generation 2 snow trekkers, especially at ski resorts, more than any other country for its size.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The capital sits in a valley ringed by high mountains, at about 1,000 metres, the highest capital in Europe; look for the Caldea tower and a sky wheel.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: A touristy eastern town packed with shops and hotels, at about 2,080 metres, has no trees on the surrounding mountains.
